text:
sam_w: Heads up — saw a regression in prefix cache hit-rate after yesterday's model rollout, looks correlated with a tiny system prompt tweak.

marta_l: numbers?

sam_w: drop from ~0.78 -> ~0.46 on the web-chat workload (p99 latency unchanged). KV miss rate jumped, warmup didn't help.

ryan_g: was tokenizer pinned in rollout?

sam_w: yes, tokenizer version same. difference was we appended a short JSON metadata block to the system prompt for tool routing.

nina_ml: hmm that matches an observation — tiny system prompt changes can shift tokenization boundaries and break exact-prefix keying.

marta_l: what keying scheme are we using currently? exact token sequence + model+tokenizer version, full prompt text for prefix keys.

ryan_g: that's fragile. two proposals: 1) aggressive canonicalization (unicode NFKC, collapse whitespace, stable JSON field ordering, drop volatile fields), or 2) compute a semantic fingerprint independent of token ids.

sam_w: we tried canonicalization before (whitespace + lowercasing) but not stable JSON ordering. Also we didn't strip low-value meta fields like session_id.

nina_ml: quick experiment idea: hash(normalize(prompt) + model_name + tokenizer_version) but use a tokenizer-agnostic normalization first: NFKC, remove timestamps/ids with regex, canonicalize JSON arrays/objects by sorting keys. Then feed that string to sha256.

marta_l: that sounds good. downside: normalization cost on the hot path. but we can do it in the warmup pipeline and cache the normalized key alongside the token-key.

ryan_g: alternative: semantic fingerprint: run a cheap sentencepiece-like normalization or small hashing embedder (128-D bloom hash) once per unique prefix during warmup. Pros: robust to small textual diffs; cons: requires model-specific calibration and adds op cost.

perf-bot: nightly-prefix-report: model-chat-v2: prefix_hit_rate=0.46, avg_fill_time=12ms, warmup_success=0.62 (yesterday)

sam_w: proposal: implement deterministic JSON canonicalizer for tool/function call sections and a small blacklist of volatile fields (session_id, timestamp, client.request_id) and re-run perf. If hit-rate still low, fall back to semantic fingerprint A/B.

marta_l: agree. we should also pin tokenizer_version in metadata and keep it as part of the key until semantic fingerprint validated. not the other way round.

ryan_g: note for infra — when canonicalization changes, keys will remap; we should add migration plan: keep dual-lookup for 7 days (old-key lookup then new-key), and backfill hot prefixes into new keys via replay from recent logs.

nina_ml: warmup strategy tweak: instead of pre-warming on first-seen token sequence, warm top-K similar prefixes using fuzzy match on fingerprint (K=50 proved useful in local tests). gives better initial hit-rate for tail variations.

marta_l: can we cheaply fuzzy match? approximate LSH on 128-bit fingerprint should be OK at scale.

perf-bot: quick-local-run: canonicalize+blacklist -> simulated hit_rate up to 0.71 on sampled web-chat traces (no tokenizer changes).

sam_w: great. action items: 1) eng-runtime to implement canonicalizer + blacklist in warmup path (ryan), 2) eng-ml to prototype 128-bit semantic fingerprint and LSH warmup cluster (nina), 3) eng-runtime + infra add dual-lookup migration and replay backfill (marta).

deploy-bot: noted — will schedule a canary rollout for the canonicalizer tomorrow in eu-west-1 with feature flag 'prefix-canon-v2'.

ryan_g: one more gotcha — function/tool call args can reorder (maps), we must canonicalize ordering or hash function signature only, not argument order.

sam_w: yep. rule: for 'tools' and 'function_call' fields, sort keys, drop ephemeral args (trace_id), and hash the function name + sorted args types/keys.

nina_ml: I'll add evaluation: measure false-positive collisions of semantic fingerprint on 10M prefixes, target collision rate < 1e-9.

marta_l: thanks team. keep thread updated with perf numbers after canary. small note: document the canonicalization rules in the runbook so support doesn't get surprised.

sam_w: putting a draft in Confluence and linking here when ready.

perf-bot: nightly-prefix-report: will post post-canary summary.
